newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gaz de France, Elf in draft cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: Gaz de France, Elf in draft cooperation pact.

text.p: French oil company Elf Aquitaine and state gas utility Gaz de France (GDF) have signed a framework accord widening cooperation between the two energy groups, a GDF spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
The accord, signed on January 24, calls for a closer partnership mainly in gas production but details will not be released until an unspecified later date, she said.
French industry sources said the two companies had been working on plans aimed at giving GDF a role in Elf's North Sea gas production in exchange for access to the gas distribution network in France.
But terms of a final accord were still being discussed.
Gaz de France is keen to expand internationally to prepare for liberalisation of the European gas sector in years ahead.
France's second oil company Total has also said it is working on specific proposals to harmonise activities with GDF both in upstream gas production and in distribution.

French newspapers, quoting union officials who had been briefed on the dialogue with Elf, said on Wednesday the deal was expected to give GDF various roles including participation in the Elgin-Franklin gas field in the British North Sea.
Elf is developing the field and expects to start producing from it in 2000.

In return Elf would have the right to import between two and three billion cubic metres of North Sea gas a year into the GDF network, representing 10 percent of annual French needs, Le Monde afternoon daily reported.
A spokesman for Elf said there had been talks but declined to give details.
"I can confirm we have been in discussions with GDF to develop projects together internationally and also to develop cooperation between the two groups," the spokesman said.
